newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka rupee ends up on state bank's dlr sales.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka rupee ends up on state bank's dlr sales.

text.p: The Sri Lanka rupee closed up against the dollar on Friday after a state bank sold large amounts of dollars in the market, dealers said.
The rupee closed at 57.72 to the dollar after opening at 57.75.
"A state name was selling dollars today. That drove the rupee up," an American Express Bank dealer said.
Some trades speculated the bank had received an inward remittance from the U.N. Compensation Commission to be paid to Sri Lankans who incurred losses during Iraq's occupation of Kuwait.
"The dollar came down from the 82 level to 68 when the state bank began to sell," said a Standard Chartered Bank dealer. "But then some import covering drove it back up to close at 72."
Overnight call money closed at 10.25 percent with the market highly liquid, dealers said.
